note: CyberChef runs libyara compiled to WebAssembly; Forge has no WASM, so the rules run on a documented subset of YARA 4 written for Forge (rule parser, string matchers and condition evaluator in TypeScript behind one private primitive, regular expressions only through the regex seam, so an untrusted recipe needs the hard kill). Supported: rule names, tags, private and global rules, meta (string, integer, boolean); text strings with ascii, wide, nocase, fullword, xor (with a range), base64 and base64wide (with an alphabet); hex strings with wildcards, nibble wildcards, ~, jumps and nested alternatives; regular expressions (classes, groups, alternation, greedy and lazy quantifiers, anchors, \b; no back references or look-around); and conditions with boolean operators, filesize, $a, #a, @a[i], !a[i], at, in, N of / any of / all of / none of / N% of with sets, for ... of and for ... in loops, int8 to uint32 reads (little and big endian), 64-bit integer arithmetic and references to earlier rules. Anything else is E_COERCE with the line and column: modules (the message names pe, elf, math, hash, ...), include, entrypoint, floating point numbers, string operators, defined, uint64, wide or xor on a regular expression. Limits: 100,000 matches per string (libyara 1,000,000), 4 MiB of input, 200 million byte steps (E_LIMIT_VALUE). The matches agree with libyara 4.5.4 (473 cases from yara-python, 366 of them random), except for hex alternatives of different length that start alike, where libyara sometimes reports the shorter path (Forge takes the first choice that lets the rest match), and Latin-1 case folding for /i on regular expressions. Output: Input matches rule "name" [metadata]. with Pattern $a, count: n and Pos n, length n, data: "..." lines for the four options (Show strings, Show string lengths, Show metadata, Show counts, as in CyberChef); the layout is from memory of CyberChef 11.5.0 and not checked against it, and 'No rules matched.' for no match is Forge's text. CyberChef puts libyara's compile errors in the output; Forge raises E_COERCE.
